messages:
Evan: short follow-up from today's infra section 1: when a region loses capacity fast, what's the canonical fallback order? spill, degrade, or return errors? cc @Marta

Marta (Infra): prefer to keep customers happy: 1) absorb with short queue (<=250ms), 2) soft-spill to nearest-region if within latency SLO, 3) swap to quantized/smaller model variant, 4) return 503+Retry-After. we'll publish concrete thresholds.

Evan: can we get the exact numeric cutoffs? teams want to automate flags.

Cal (SRE): from last canary: queue.p95 > 400ms was the tipping point that triggered spill. observed median +35ms, p95 +110ms on spill. log snippet:

```
2026-03-25T14:02:11Z spot: reclaim 34%
2026-03-25T14:02:12Z queue.p95 412ms -> spill->eu-west1
```

Dina (Product): product asks for a per-project opt-out for cross-region spill (residency) and a UI estimate of the latency penalty before enabling.

Marta (Infra): agreed. plan: add routing-policy flag + audit events next sprint; UI toggle sprint after. I'll draft a one-pager playbook with thresholds (suggested: spill if region capacity < 12% OR queue.p95 > 400ms; degrade only if spill blocked or cross-region latency > 150ms).

Cal (SRE): action items: add telemetry keys spill.reason and spill.dest_region, alert if spill.rate > 0.5% sustained 5m, and add 90s cooldown after failed burst-to-dedicated to avoid thrash.

AuditBot: Audit requirement noted: log origin_region, dest_region, timestamp, and request_ids on spill events.

Evan: thanks 1. Can teams hold off enabling cross-region by default until playbook + toggle land?

Marta (Infra): yes please hold off in prod. experiments are fine. posting draft by Monday and scheduling a short sync.

OpsBot: Follow-up meeting scheduled: "Regional Fallback Playbook" Mon 10:00 PT. Invite sent.

Evan: appreciate the quick answers. :thumbsup:
